liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Stranger among the finest they have heard; David Gans played this Stranger on the Grateful Dead Hour on KFOG the following week [21][29]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (2 reviews): Attendee recalls the surprise of Dear Mr. Fantasy leading into Hey Jude, then Watchtower; Reviewer urges listening to Dear Mr. Fantasy first and not skipping the late second set [25][30]
- **Loose Lucy** (1 review): Loose Lucy rocks, and Jerry cuts loose at the end [21]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy described as a scorcher [29]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (1 review): Reviewer considers this perhaps the finest all-around Victim or the Crime, with a twisted segue [29]
- **All Along The Watchtower** (1 review): After the tackle, Jerry stepped back, raised his eyebrows, then played a particularly nasty stretch of solo [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-06-09.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-6936.34398.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd90-06-09.sbd-matrix.miller-ladner.6936.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 161 min; rated 3.44/5 by 16 [2]. Said about its sound: Matrix is very clear, with just enough audience noise to convey the party atmosphere; Reviewer says this matrix sounds very nice [19][28]
- **gd1990-06-09.149721.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min [3]
- **gd1990-06-09.149620.ultramatrix.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min [5]
- **gd90-06-09.bk4011.nickspicks.23532.sbeok.flac**: source not stated; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this among the best-sounding audience recordings, helped by Cal Expo's small size [24]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the crowd energy was huge and Cal Expo was a one-of-a-kind place [19]
- Reviewer's first show after moving to California, when the Greek and Frost were no longer within reach [20]
- A man rushed from the crowd toward Jerry during Watchtower; a roadie tackled him just short of Jerry [22]
- Reviewer says their friend charged the stage at Jerry hoping to merge with him; security grabbed and ejected him [26]
- Reviewer counts this among the best shows of the 1990 summer run [21]
- Reviewer places this run among the hottest of 1990, with strong sound and performances [24]
- Attendee of all three June 1990 Cal Expo shows rates Saturday's second set the best [25]
- Reviewer calls this one of the best setlists of the 1990 summer [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-06-09.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-6936.34398.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD (Matrix) > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHN - Seamless fix of shn id 6936 [1]. Also: Fixed version: disc 2 to disc 3 transition made seamless using reverse fades and matched splice volumes in Cool Edit 2000 [1]
- **gd90-06-09.sbd-matrix.miller-ladner.6936.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD (Matrix) > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHN [2]. Also: Audience patch at end of encore by Ken Adelman, using Schoeps CMC441 mics into Sony PCM F1 [2]
- **gd1990-06-09.149721.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 19, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [3]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several master sets combined to complete the show [3]
- **gd1990-06-09.149620.ultramatrix.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 19, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [5]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several master sets combined to complete the show [5]
- **gd90-06-09.bk4011.nickspicks.23532.sbeok.flac**: source: B&K 4011 110degrees ORTF on the "Mike Stand" 6'4" Neumann p48 phantom supply > Sony TCD-D10 pro II (48k) > DAT master > TAscam DA-20 MKII > Marigo Audio Lab… [7]. Also: Audience recording made with BK 4011 microphones [24]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead BGP Laminate, Cal Expo Amphitheatre](https://www.dead.net/archives/1990/artwork/bgp-laminate-cal-expo-amphitheatre) [32]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Cal Expo Amphitheatre - June 10, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/june-10-1990) [33]

Reviewer's first show after moving to California, when the Greek and Frost were no longer within reach
Reviewer ranks this Stranger among the finest they have heard
Loose Lucy rocks, and Jerry cuts loose at the end
Reviewer counts this among the best shows of the 1990 summer run
A man rushed from the crowd toward Jerry during Watchtower; a roadie tackled him just short of Jerry
After the tackle, Jerry stepped back, raised his eyebrows, then played a particularly nasty stretch of solo
Reviewer calls this among the best-sounding audience recordings, helped by Cal Expo's small size
Audience recording made with BK 4011 microphones
Reviewer places this run among the hottest of 1990, with strong sound and performances
Attendee of all three June 1990 Cal Expo shows rates Saturday's second set the best
Attendee recalls the surprise of Dear Mr. Fantasy leading into Hey Jude, then Watchtower
Reviewer says their friend charged the stage at Jerry hoping to merge with him; security grabbed and ejected him
Reviewer says this matrix sounds very nice
Reviewer calls this one of the best setlists of the 1990 summer
David Gans played this Stranger on the Grateful Dead Hour on KFOG the following week
Cassidy described as a scorcher
Reviewer considers this perhaps the finest all-around Victim or the Crime, with a twisted segue
Reviewer urges listening to Dear Mr. Fantasy first and not skipping the late second set
Fixed version: disc 2 to disc 3 transition made seamless using reverse fades and matched splice volumes in Cool Edit 2000
Matrix lineage: soundboard matrix to DAT, CDR, WAV, then SHN
Audience patch at end of encore by Ken Adelman, using Schoeps CMC441 mics into Sony PCM F1
Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several master sets combined to complete the show
Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several master sets combined to complete the show
